stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and null spec. 'Live Preview of Content in CMS' is a complex feature involving real-time rendering, draft/published state management, preview access security, and performance considerations. Openspec should elaborate requirements and propose meaningful AC first; speckit then hardens with testability criteria, security checks, and edge case coverage.

agentContributions.notes: Story requests Live Preview of Content in CMS — a novel capability. The central attachment point is useContent (236 callers), which is the sole content-fetching hook every Contentstack component routes through via getContentByKey. Enabling Live Preview requires this hook (and the Contentstack client it wraps) to support switching between Delivery and Preview APIs based on preview-mode context. The Contentstack client initialization (likely in a provider or SDK config file not shown here) is also an attachment point. VCs are derived entirely from the description since ACs are empty.

Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria with useful notes identifying useContent (236 callers) and the Contentstack client as attachment points. I created all 12 ACs from scratch based on the story title, description, and file paths. File contents were NOT available (paths only), so ACs are derived from the behavioral requirements implied by 'Live Preview of Content in CMS' and the known Contentstack integration points. AC-1/AC-2 cover the core preview vs. delivery switching. AC-3 covers live refresh without reload. AC-4/AC-5/AC-6/AC-10 cover error and edge cases. AC-7 is a security gate ensuring preview credentials never leak to production. AC-8/AC-9 cover runtime mode transitions. AC-11 covers concurrent fetch isolation. AC-12 covers referenced content depth. If file contents had been available, I might have refined these further based on existing error-handling patterns and the contentCard interface shape.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Openspec identified attachment points (useContent with 236 callers, Contentstack client) but did not elaborate requirements or propose acceptance criteria — it stopped at reconnaissance. Speckit then performed openspec's job by creating 12 ACs from scratch, which is a role inversion of the sequential pipeline (elaborate → harden). Both agents report acceptanceChanged: false, yet speckit claims it 'created all 12 ACs,' creating a contradiction — either the ACs were never persisted or the claim is aspirational. Additionally, both agents note file contents were unavailable (only paths), limiting the quality of derived ACs. Non-overlapping value exists but only because openspec left a gap speckit filled. Human review needed to verify ACs were actually persisted and to confirm pipeline role adherence on re-run.
